price.basis: billed by tokens alone, with no per-search fee: deepseek-flash input $0.15 off-peak / $0.30 peak and output $0.60 / $1.20 per million tokens (cache hits $0.003 / $0.006); the search's own extra model requests are billed as tokens too, so the evaluation records the measured token cost per call

reachability.note: DeepSeek's official API is a mainland-China service; its pages state no regional restriction.

deepseek-anthropic-api.note: Base URL https://api.deepseek.com/anthropic; `x-api-key` Fully Supported and `anthropic-version` Ignored. The field-compatibility table lists the content blocks `server_tool_use` Supported and `web_search_tool_result` Supported (`search_result`, `mcp_tool_use`, `mcp_tool_result` Not Supported, `mcp_servers` Ignored); its `tools` rows cover `name`, `input_schema`, `description` (Fully Supported) and `cache_control` (Ignored) and name no tool `type`, so no server tool type string is stated on this page.

deepseek-claude-code-web-search.source: DeepSeek official Claude Code integration guide, api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/agent_integrations/claude_code
deepseek-claude-code-web-search.note: "The DeepSeek API natively supports the Web Search feature in Claude Code … if the model determines that your question requires a web search, it will invoke the Web Search tool and perform the search through the API provided by DeepSeek. Because invoking the Web Search tool generates additional LLM API requests … additional model token costs will be incurred." The tool type Claude Code sends is not named.

deepseek-pricing.source: DeepSeek official models and pricing page, api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing
deepseek-pricing.note: Token prices per million for deepseek-flash: cache-hit input $0.003 / $0.006, cache-miss input $0.15 / $0.30, output $0.60 / $1.20 (off-peak / peak); no per-search charge is listed.

openQuestions: The server tool type is not named by DeepSeek. The evaluation sends Anthropic's `web_search_20250305` server tool on `deepseek-flash`; whether the endpoint runs it for a client other than Claude Code is what the measurement settles, and its outcome is this backend's verdict.
notes: DeepSeek server-side web_search reading (Issue #883): listed — the Anthropic-compatible endpoint documents the server-tool result blocks as Supported and its Claude Code guide says web search runs through DeepSeek's API, but no page names the tool type or states the feature for a generic Anthropic client.
Searching here costs model tokens on the same DeepSeek key the production route uses, and the query reaches a model before any search; the evaluation sends only the public query.
